title: 4yo M Drowning (Irrigation Canal)
chiefComplaint: Pulled unresponsive from an irrigation canal
background: Found floating face down in the irrigation canal behind the family house. Estimated submersion 5 to 8 minutes, unwitnessed. His 11 year old sister pulled him out and a neighbour gave compressions with no rescue breaths for about 6 minutes until the ambulance arrived. Return of spontaneous circulation was achieved in the ambulance after two cycles and one adrenaline dose. Weight estimated at 16 kg. Drowning is the leading cause of death in Thai children aged 1 to 14, and the peak is April and the school holidays.

exam.finding: Small child, unresponsive, wet and cold, mottled and cyanosed, agonal respirations at 8/min, canal weed in his hair

Frothy pink fluid at the mouth and nose, silt and vegetation in the oropharynx requiring suction, pupils 5 mm and sluggish bilaterally, no head injury palpable, cervical collar applied because the mechanism is unwitnessed

Sinus tachycardia at 168/min post arrest, weak central pulses, capillary refill 5 seconds, cold peripheries. In hypothermia, pulses are hard to feel and you must check for a full minute before declaring arrest
Widespread coarse crackles in all zones, poor chest expansion, wheeze, oxygen saturations 82% on 15 L/min via mask. Surfactant washout, not water in the lungs, is what impairs gas exchange
Distended with swallowed water and air from bag-mask ventilation, soft, no bruising to suggest inflicted injury, bowel sounds present
Cold, mottled and cyanosed, core temperature 33.8 C, no bruising of different ages, no burns, no marks suggesting non-accidental injury

GCS 6 (E1V2M3), flaccid tone, no seizure activity at present, pupils sluggish. Neurological prognosis in drowning is decided by hypoxic time and cannot be assessed reliably for 72 hours, particularly while hypothermic

investigations.name: Arterial blood gas
investigations.report: Severe mixed acidosis with profound hypoxaemia after a hypoxic arrest. Lactate above 10 after paediatric drowning is associated with poor neurological outcome but is not on its own a reason to stop.

investigations.name: Capillary glucose
investigations.report: Hypoglycaemia. Small children have limited glycogen stores and deplete them fast during an arrest. Both hypoglycaemia and hyperglycaemia worsen hypoxic brain injury.

investigations.name: Portable Chest X-ray
investigations.report: Diffuse bilateral perihilar and basal airspace opacification consistent with aspiration and pulmonary oedema. Endotracheal tube tip 1 cm above the carina, needs withdrawing 1.5 cm. Gastric distension. No pneumothorax, no rib fractures.

investigations.name: Core (oesophageal) temperature
investigations.report: Moderate hypothermia. Do not rewarm above 36 C. Targeted temperature management at 33 to 36 C for 24 to 48 hours is the standard after paediatric cardiac arrest, and active rewarming to normal is harmful.

investigations.name: Potassium and sodium
investigations.report: Mild hypokalaemia, common in hypothermia as potassium shifts intracellularly. It will rise on rewarming, so replace cautiously.

investigations.name: 12-Lead ECG
investigations.report: Sinus tachycardia at 166/min with a prolonged QTc of 480 ms and an Osborn J wave in the inferior and lateral leads, consistent with hypothermia. Hypothermic myocardium is irritable, so handle and move the child gently.

data.label: Airway, suction and oxygenation come first in drowning
actions: Bag-valve-mask with 15 L/min oxygen and PEEP

doseMap.Bag-valve-mask with 15 L/min oxygen and: Drowning is a hypoxic arrest, so ventilation is the priority and the algorithm is airway first, unlike adult cardiac arrest. Do not attempt abdominal thrusts to expel water, they cause aspiration

data.label: Rapid sequence intubation with lung protective ventilation
actions: Nasogastric tube to decompress the stomach

doseMap.Ketamine and rocuronium: Ketamine 2 mg/kg (32 mg) and rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg (19 mg). Ketamine preserves blood pressure in a shocked child
doseMap.PEEP 8-10 cmH2O: Tidal volume 6-8 mL/kg. Surfactant washout means this behaves like ARDS

doseMap.Dextrose bolus: 2 mL/kg of 10% dextrose (32 mL), recheck in 30 min
doseMap.Cautious isotonic fluid bolus: 10 mL/kg (160 mL) with reassessment. Large volumes worsen pulmonary oedema in drowning

data.label: Oxygenation improves
data.narrative: With PEEP and 100% oxygen, saturations rise to 94% over ten minutes. Perfusion improves after the fluid bolus and dextrose. He remains deeply unconscious, which at this stage tells you nothing about outcome.

data.label: Speak to the 11 year old sister who pulled him out (Empathy)
data.narrative: The parents are being managed by the nurses. The sister is sitting alone outside the resus room, still wet, and she has heard someone say he might not wake up. You crouch down and tell her that the compressions she and the neighbour gave are the reason his heart is beating now, and that whatever happens next was decided in the canal and not by her. Pi Ek says afterwards that in twenty-eight years the sibling is the person nobody ever talks to, and the one most likely to still be carrying it at thirty.

data.label: Targeted temperature management, no aggressive rewarming

doseMap.Passive rewarming to 34-36 C only: Do not rewarm past 36 C. Fever after hypoxic brain injury measurably worsens outcome and is the one thing you can definitely control

data.label: Paediatric ICU transfer and safeguarding assessment

doseMap.No prophylactic antibiotics or steroids: Neither improves outcome in drowning. Treat infection when it is proven, guided by culture. Canal water is dirty but prophylaxis still does not work

data.label: 48 hour course
data.narrative: Extubated on day 4. He follows commands on day 5 with a mild left hemiparesis and expressive difficulty. Neurology expects substantial but incomplete recovery over six months. The eight minute submersion is doing the talking now, not anything that happened in your department.

data.label: Disposition
data.narrative: Discharged to rehabilitation at three weeks. The canal behind the house has no fence and neither of the two adults at home can swim. A referral goes to the district health office for the survival swimming programme, which is the only intervention in this whole case with population level evidence behind it.
